domain: Religious Studies / Ritual Theory / Collective Memory
topic_summary: Analysis of Tisha B'Av and Passover as ritual catastrophe-memory practices in Judaism, examining whether commemorative reading preserves survival-competence (D5) or only mourning-practice and boundary-norms (D1/D4). Both rituals encode responses to catastrophic loss (Temple destruction, Egyptian slavery), but differ structurally in whether they transmit adaptive capacity or only preserve memorial obligation.

key_entities: Tisha B'Av (annual mourning ritual for Temple destructions and subsequent tragedies)
Passover/Pesach (liberation commemoration with seder ritual and Haggadah recitation)
Temple sacrificial system (destroyed 70 CE, never restored)
Haggadah (liturgical text encoding Exodus narrative and interpretive framework)
key_tensions: Mourning-practice vs survival-competence (D1/D4 vs D5 classification contest)
Restrictive observance (Tisha B'Av prohibitions) vs performative enactment (Passover seder)
Centralized Temple worship vs decentralized text-study and home ritual
key_mechanisms: Intergenerational transmission via ritual performance and textual recitation
Rabbinic transformation of sacrifice-centered worship into text-centered practice
Embodied rehearsal of survival conditions through seder performance
Boundary-maintenance through negative observance (Tisha B'Av) vs positive enactment (Passover)
key_absences: Comparative analysis with other diaspora survival mechanisms (e.g., Babylonian exile adaptations)
Quantitative data on ritual observance rates and intergenerational transmission success

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Ritual catastrophe-memory as mechanism for collective survival across millennia without territorial sovereignty or centralized institutions
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Rabbinic interpretive tradition grounded in textual fidelity and communal practice-norms

readings.commitment: Ritual preserves mourning-practice and boundary-norms (D1/D4) — commemorative reading maintains group identity through memorial obligation
readings.authority_grounding: Rabbinic codification of restrictive observance and liturgical lament
readings.expected_structural_delta: Tisha B'Av as pure D1/D4 — ritual IS the boundary-maintenance, no survival-competence transmission

readings.commitment: Ritual preserves survival-competence (D5) — commemorative reading transmits adaptive capacity for institutional transformation and decentralized continuity
readings.authority_grounding: Rabbinic transformation of Temple-centered worship into portable text-study framework
readings.expected_structural_delta: Passover as D5 — ritual teaches how to survive catastrophe through embodied rehearsal and knowledge transmission

readings.commitment: Ritual encodes both mourning-practice AND survival-competence (D1/D4 + D5) — commemorative reading preserves loss-memory while transmitting adaptive mechanisms
readings.authority_grounding: Post-Temple rabbinic synthesis combining restrictive observance with performative enactment
readings.expected_structural_delta: Passover as hybrid — bitter herbs (D1/D4 mourning) + seder performance (D5 survival rehearsal) in single ritual structure

axiom_contradictions.basis: Mourning-practice reading holds that ritual function is complete when memorial obligation is fulfilled (boundary-maintenance through negative observance); survival-competence reading holds that ritual function requires transmission of adaptive capacity (institutional transformation through positive enactment). No single framework can hold both as the complete account of ritual function.

axes.structural_delta: Ritual catastrophe-memory functions to preserve group identity through memorial obligation and restrictive observance, not to transmit survival-competence
axes.primary_observable: Tisha B'Av observance structure: prohibitions (fasting, no leather, no joy), liturgical lament (Lamentations, kinnot), absence of performative survival rehearsal
axes.selection_reason: First reading in kernel contest — establishes D1/D4 baseline for comparison

axes.structural_delta: Ritual catastrophe-memory functions to transmit adaptive capacity for institutional transformation and decentralized continuity without territorial sovereignty
axes.primary_observable: Passover seder structure: embodied rehearsal (eating bitter herbs, reclining as free people), intergenerational knowledge transmission (Haggadah recitation, four questions), post-Temple adaptation (home-centered vs Temple-centered)
axes.selection_reason: Second reading in kernel contest — establishes D5 claim with distinct observable and beneficiary structure

axes.structural_delta: Ritual catastrophe-memory encodes both mourning-practice and survival-competence in single structure — commemorative reading preserves loss-memory while transmitting adaptive mechanisms
axes.primary_observable: Passover dual structure: restrictive elements (no leavened bread, bitter herbs as slavery reminder) + performative elements (seder as Exodus rehearsal, Haggadah as portable institutional framework)
axes.selection_reason: Third reading in kernel contest — highest centrality, synthesizes mourning and survival dimensions

axes.structural_delta: Post-Temple rabbinic transformation from sacrifice-centered to text-centered worship enables survival without territorial sovereignty
axes.primary_observable: Synagogue proliferation post-70 CE, Haggadah standardization, home-based ritual performance rates
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: upstream mountain to survival-competence reading but lower structural distinctiveness than kernel readings

axes.structural_delta: Ritual performance as mechanism for preserving knowledge across generations without institutional continuity
axes.primary_observable: Haggadah recitation rates, four questions tradition, observance persistence across diaspora communities
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: mechanism shared across readings, captured in primary observables of selected axes

deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Upstream mountain to survival-competence reading but captured in primary observables of selected readings

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Ritual performance as knowledge preservation mechanism
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Transmission mechanism shared across all readings, not structurally independent

omegas.description: Does Tisha B'Av contain latent D5 elements not captured in mourning-practice reading? Post-Temple rabbinic adaptation itself demonstrates survival-competence, but ritual structure is purely restrictive. Possible reclassification if communal reflection on 'baseless hatred' functions as conflict-resolution training.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) + mourning_practice_reading classification

omegas.description: How do Jewish ritual catastrophe-memory mechanisms compare to other diaspora survival systems (Armenian Genocide commemoration, African diaspora ritual, Tibetan exile practices)? Is D1/D4 vs D5 distinction universal or culturally specific?
omegas.source: Absence Inventory + Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan)

omegas.description: If Passover observance rates decline in secular populations, does survival-competence transmission fail or migrate to non-ritual forms? Possible reclassification from D5 to D1/D4 if adaptive capacity no longer transmitted through ritual performance.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 1 (Operational Medium) + survival_competence_reading validity

omegas.description: Do the three readings actually instantiate different constraints, or do they collapse into one constraint read from different observer positions? Hybrid reading may subsume the other two if mourning and survival are inseparable in actual ritual performance.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel structure sorts cleanly: mourning_practice_reading captures Tisha B'Av (pure D1/D4), survival_competence_reading captures Passover D5 dimension, hybrid_transformation_reading captures Passover dual structure. Research context confirms structural distinction between restrictive observance and performative enactment.
